entries.description: logical maximum batch size (default: 2048) (env: LLAMA_ARG_BATCH)
entries.notes: Aliased onto --prefill-chunk-size, the logical prefill batch, which has an observable effect on chunked prefill; the resolution is pinned by resolve_prefill_chunk_size tests and the resolved value is reported as `n_batch` in /props (src/server/routes/props_tests.rs). It is not b10621's n_batch: the unset default differs (512, mlxcel's --prefill-chunk-size default, against 2048) and mlxcel schedules chunked prefill rather than filling a llama_batch, so a given value does not produce the same per-forward token count. Changing mlxcel's own default to 2048 is a throughput decision deliberately not made inside a compatibility issue (#1472).

entries.description: save idle slots to the prompt cache on new task, and clear them when using unified KV (default: enabled, requires cache-ram) (env: LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_IDLE_SLOTS)
entries.notes: Declared on both binaries since #1473 so the refusal is a diagnostic rather than clap's unknown-argument error: no per-slot retained prompt exists to save when a slot goes idle: reuse is a process-wide radix trie over token prefixes that every request consults regardless of which sequence last held the tokens, and it already survives a slot going idle, which is the effect the flag buys upstream. The inert value (--no-cache-idle-slots, or a falsy LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_IDLE_SLOTS) is accepted; a request for the behavior is refused at startup with a diagnostic naming what is missing.
divergence: a request for the behavior is refused at startup with a diagnostic; only the inert value is accepted

entries.description: whether to enable prompt caching (default: enabled) (env: LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_PROMPT)
entries.notes: Spelling, env binding and upstream's enabled default, and since #1473 the same prompt-prefix cache on every text route: /v1/completions and native /completion build a raw-prompt cache request context (build_raw_prompt_cache_context) through the same seam the chat-shaped routes use, keyed on the model id and a raw-prompt template signature so a raw prompt never adopts a chat-rendered prefix. mlxcel also ships its own --no-prompt-cache, and between two explicit operator disables the disable wins; that interaction is invisible to a b10621 client, which has no such flag, so it is recorded here rather than as a divergence.

entries.description: set the maximum cache size in MiB (default: 8192, -1 - no limit, 0 - disable)[(more info)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/16391) (env: LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_RAM)
entries.notes: Aliased onto --prompt-cache-capacity-bytes: the value is read in MiB with upstream's -1 (no limit) and 0 (disable) sentinels and converted to the same byte budget, and --prompt-cache-capacity-bytes wins when both are given. A requested value is therefore honored exactly; what differs is the unset default, which stays at mlxcel's own 2048 MiB because changing a memory default is a deployment decision deliberately not made inside a compatibility issue (#1473). Since #1473 the budget bounds the cache on every text route, not just the chat-shaped ones, and -cram rewrites through the argv pre-pass.
divergence: the unset default is 2048 MiB (mlxcel's --prompt-cache-capacity-bytes default); b10621 defaults to 8192

entries.description: min chunk size to attempt reusing from the cache via KV shifting, requires prompt caching to be enabled (default: 0) [(card)](https://ggml.ai/f0.png) (env: LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_REUSE)
entries.notes: Upstream's default of 0 is accepted; a positive minimum chunk size is refused at startup with a diagnostic naming the missing operation. The classification is permanent, decided in #1473 against the cache invariant rather than deferred: a key written at monotonic position p is rotated at p at write time and never re-rotated, and every operation preserves that (trim_front_keep_sink advances live_start instead of decrementing offset; gather_positions and gather_within_tail compact surviving slots without re-rotating them). KV-shift chunk reuse renumbers the tail of a cached span, so it needs a rotation primitive threaded with each layer's RoPE descriptor, a dequantize-rotate-requantize pass for Int8, sidecar rebuilds the Turbo modes already decline for a head trim, and a second implementation against the paged block table. The strict-prefix radix cache covers the common shared-prefix case that motivates the flag upstream.
divergence: a positive minimum chunk size is refused at startup instead of enabling KV-shift reuse; only the upstream default of 0 is accepted
no KV operation re-bases the rotary positions of a cached span, so chunk reuse cannot be expressed at all

entries.notes: Declared on both binaries since #1473 so the refusal is a diagnostic rather than clap's unknown-argument error: There are no successive context checkpoints for a minimum spacing to separate; see --ctx-checkpoints. 0 is accepted as the explicit no-minimum spelling and any other value, including upstream's default of 8192, is refused at startup with a diagnostic naming the absent ring. -cms rewrites through the argv pre-pass.

entries.description: whether to enable continuous batching (a.k.a dynamic batching) (default: enabled) (env: LLAMA_ARG_CONT_BATCHING)
entries.notes: Spelling, env binding and upstream's enabled default, with -cb and -nocb rewritten by the argv pre-pass since #1473. --no-cont-batching resolves to --max-batch-size 1, and the scheduler now ands its mixed-step gate with max_batch_size > 1, so disabling stops prefill/decode interleaving outright rather than only pinning the decode width. That is upstream's own gate: b10621 adds pending prompts to the batch only when `params_base.cont_batching || batch.size() == 0` (server-context.cpp), which leaves its slots, prompt cache and speculative decoding in place exactly as mlxcel does.

entries.description: whether to use context shift on infinite text generation (default: disabled) (env: LLAMA_ARG_CONTEXT_SHIFT)
entries.notes: Both spellings and LLAMA_ARG_CONTEXT_SHIFT accepted, with upstream's disabled default. Disabled, an over-long prompt is refused at admission with upstream's exceed-context wording and a generation that reaches the per-slot bound stops with truncated: true and stop_type: "limit" (b10621's process_token guard); enabled, the scheduler front-discards past the sequence's resolved n_keep prefix, raising the discard to the prefill-chunk overshoot when needed. Before #1472 the shift was unconditional (a fixed 4-token attention sink) whenever --ctx-size or --max-kv-size bounded the window; docs/llama-server-compat.md carries the migration note. Mode caveats, both mlxcel-only surfaces: the trim is a recorded no-op on Turbo-quantized layers (KVCache::trim_front_keep_sink support matrix, warned at startup), and VLM sequences are exempt from the machinery exactly as upstream disables ctx_shift under multimodal.

entries.description: add a control vector note: use comma-separated values to add multiple control vectors
entries.notes: Activation steering has no mlxcel application path: MLX model forwards do not add per-layer steering directions, and accepting a vector without applying it would silently change what the deployment believes it is serving. The flag parses (hidden) and any configured vector fails startup before the model load with a diagnostic naming logit-level steering (--lang-bias / per-request logit_bias) as the nearest mlxcel feature. Because no vector configuration can ever serve, partial application and cross-configuration prompt/KV cache reuse are impossible by construction.
divergence: b10621 loads the vector and applies it to the model's activations; mlxcel rejects the flag at startup before any weight is read.

entries.notes: Declared on both binaries since #1473 so the refusal is a diagnostic rather than clap's unknown-argument error: mlxcel captures at most one snapshot per sequence, at the prompt/generation boundary (capture_history_boundary_snapshot), and has no ring of per-slot context checkpoints to size. 0 is accepted as the explicit disable; any other value, including upstream's default of 32, is refused at startup with a diagnostic. --swa-checkpoints is accepted as the same spelling and -ctxcp rewrites through the argv pre-pass.

entries.description: size of the prompt context (default: 0, 0 = loaded from model) (env: LLAMA_ARG_CTX_SIZE)
entries.notes: Same semantics: 0 = derive from the model, and the total is shared across slots (ctx_size / slots) exactly as llama-server splits n_ctx across n_parallel. The resolved per-slot window is now reported as `n_ctx` in /props and logged at startup.

entries.description: number of tokens to keep from the initial prompt (default: 0, -1 = all)
entries.notes: Accepted as the server-wide default for the retained prefix on a context shift, including the -1 = retain-the-whole-initial-prompt form, overridable per request as n_keep. The resolution mirrors b10621's slot arithmetic: -1 resolves to the prompt length, one token is added when the tokenizer prepended BOS, and the value is clamped to bound - 4 at trim time (upstream's n_ctx - 4). Replaces the fixed MAX_KV_SIZE_SINK_KEEP = 4 attention sink; pass --context-shift --keep 4 to reproduce the pre-#1472 rolling window.

entries.default: enabled if number of slots is auto
entries.description: use single unified KV buffer shared across all sequences (default: enabled if number of slots is auto) (env: LLAMA_ARG_KV_UNIFIED)
entries.notes: Declared on both binaries since #1473 so the refusal is a diagnostic rather than clap's unknown-argument error: KV is allocated per sequence through the scheduler's cache pool, which divides --ctx-size into per-slot shares; there is no unified shared buffer to switch to. --no-kv-unified (and -no-kvu) is accepted as the inert spelling of mlxcel's only layout, and a request for the unified buffer is refused at startup with a diagnostic that points at --parallel 1 for the whole-context case. See the --parallel entry, whose by_design divergence is the auto default's other half.
divergence: a request for the behavior is refused at startup with a diagnostic; only the inert value is accepted

entries.description: number of server slots (default: -1, -1 = auto) (env: LLAMA_ARG_N_PARALLEL)
entries.notes: Spelling, env, -np and b10621's whole value domain: the default is -1 (auto) and auto resolves to 4 slots, which is upstream's own auto resolution (server-context.cpp: "n_parallel is set to auto, using n_parallel = 4 and kv_unified = true"). What differs permanently is the second half of that upstream line. Upstream's auto also switches to one unified KV buffer shared by the slots, so a default-config single request can use the whole context; mlxcel's scheduler owns a cache pool that allocates KV per sequence and divides --ctx-size into per-slot shares, and --kv-unified is not_applicable for the same reason. An operator who wants one request to have the whole context passes --parallel 1, which is the same allocation upstream's unified buffer gives that request.
divergence: b10621's auto default also enables a unified KV buffer shared by the slots, so a default-config single request may use the whole context; mlxcel keeps per-slot context shares (see --kv-unified)

rationale.reason: The KV layout is a property of the scheduler cache pool, which allocates and reclaims per sequence so a slot can be freed and reused independently; a shared buffer would make one sequence's footprint depend on its neighbours' liveness. The slot count itself matches upstream exactly, and --parallel 1 reproduces the whole-context allocation upstream's unified buffer gives a single request.
rationale.revisit_if: the paged cache pool gains a cross-sequence context budget, so an idle slot's unused share can be lent to an active sequence without breaking per-sequence reclamation

entries.description: number of tokens to predict (default: -1, -1 = infinity) (env: LLAMA_ARG_N_PREDICT)
entries.notes: Both spellings (--predict, --n-predict) accepted; default -1 = until EOS/context, matching llama-server per request.

entries.description: RoPE base frequency, used by NTK-aware scaling (default: loaded from model) (env: LLAMA_ARG_ROPE_FREQ_BASE)
entries.notes: Replaces the checkpoint's rope_theta before the model is constructed, and feeds the llama3 band arithmetic as well as the plain rotation, so the frequency table and the stored base cannot drift apart. On Gemma 3 it reaches the global-attention layers only; the sliding layers keep rope_local_base_freq, which is llama.cpp's separate rope_freq_base_train_swa.

entries.description: RoPE frequency scaling factor, expands context by a factor of 1/N (env: LLAMA_ARG_ROPE_FREQ_SCALE)
entries.notes: b10621's `rope_freq_scale = N`. Applied as a linear scheme when the checkpoint names no scheme or names "default"/"linear", matching the flag's own "defaults to linear unless specified by the model". On a checkpoint that declares a banded scheme (llama3) a bare scale is refused: b10621 multiplies its rope_freq_scale into that rotation and mlxcel's llama3 table has no such multiplier, so composing them would change the rotation in a way neither side describes.

entries.description: RoPE context scaling factor, expands context by a factor of N (env: LLAMA_ARG_ROPE_SCALE)
entries.notes: b10621's `rope_freq_scale = 1/N`, normalized at the CLI edge so `--rope-scale 8` and `--rope-freq-scale 0.125` are one stored value. Passing both with values that are not reciprocals is refused rather than resolved by precedence, because clap gives mlxcel two independent options where b10621 has one field that the later flag simply overwrites.

entries.description: RoPE frequency scaling method, defaults to linear unless specified by the model (env: LLAMA_ARG_ROPE_SCALING_TYPE)
entries.notes: Same value domain {none,linear,yarn} and the same LLAMA_ARG_ROPE_SCALING_TYPE binding. All three are applied to the checkpoint's rope_scaling block before the model is constructed, so before any KV cache exists; `yarn` (since #1472) builds the YaRN frequency table on the shared RoPE path, with the factor from --rope-scale / --rope-freq-scale and the --yarn-* knobs. An override that reaches no RoPE code path refuses to serve rather than starting (models::rope_overrides::verify_applied), and a family whose own RoPE path cannot represent the requested scheme (Gemma 3's linear-only global rope, InternLM's dynamic-NTK resolver) refuses with a load error naming the scheme.

entries.description: how much the prompt of a request must match the prompt of a slot in order to use that slot (default: 0.10, 0.0 = disabled)

Upstream's own default is 0.10, so an explicitly passed default is refused rather than silently honored as a slot-selection policy that does not exist; 0 is accepted as the explicit disable.

entries.description: use full-size SWA cache (default: false) [(more info)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/13194#issuecomment-2868343055) (env: LLAMA_ARG_SWA_FULL)
entries.notes: Accepted at its inert default (false, also LLAMA_ARG_SWA_FULL=0), and refused at startup when set: sliding-window families (Gemma 3/4, Exaone 4, gpt-oss, RecurrentGemma, Step 3.5, Mellum, Ministral 3, AFMoE, DeepSeek V4) build their own ring caches from the checkpoint's sliding_window inside each model's cache constructor, and mlxcel has no full-size SWA cache mode for the flag to select. The capability the flag purchases upstream (KV state save/restore and context shifting over SWA layers) is gated on those caches being scheduler-owned, not on the ring's size, so widening the ring would spend the memory without buying the feature. The diagnostic names the families and the inert spelling.

entries.description: YaRN: scale sqrt(t) or attention magnitude (default: -1.00) (env: LLAMA_ARG_YARN_ATTN_FACTOR)
entries.notes: Spelling and env accepted, and since #1472 a non-sentinel value tunes the rotation: the shared RoPE path builds a YaRN frequency table (RopeScalingKind::Yarn) and the knobs overlay it wherever a YaRN rotation is in force, whether --rope-scaling yarn forced it or the checkpoint's own rope_scaling block declares it. With a non-YaRN rotation in force the knobs are inert, exactly as in b10621, whose llama_context reads them only under LLAMA_ROPE_SCALING_TYPE_YARN. The families that implement YaRN outside the shared seam (DeepSeek V2/V3.2/V4, gpt-oss, Mellum, TeleChat3) build it from their own config; an override installed against one of them refuses to serve (models::rope_overrides::verify_applied) rather than being ignored. Participates only when the resolved extrapolation mix is 0: with a non-zero mix b10621's llama-context.cpp recomputes the attention factor over the flag, and mlxcel mirrors that resolution order.

entries.description: Number of tokens after n_keep that may be discarded when shifting context (0 = half context)
